title: at green --help asserts a guard the tool does not enforce
body:
`intent at green --help` prints `Set an AT green (reachable only from red)`. The tool does not enforce it: `at green` accepts any status from any status, and a `to-write` test goes straight to `green` at rc=0.

DRIVEN, NOT REASONED. Hit by vc on 2026-08-29 minting ST0068's own acceptance tests -- `at green ST0068 AT-01.1` succeeded from `to-write` while the documentation page written an hour earlier said it could not. Reproduced against the delivered binary `3.0.0 (8177b53e)`. cc confirmed independently.

THE REGISTER ALREADY CARRIES THE CONTRADICTION, IN THREE FIELDS OF ONE ROW, EACH CORRECT IN ISOLATION. `help` asserts the precondition. `target.ratification` says the opposite in terms: "v2 refuses green unless the AT is currently red (bin/intent_acceptance:1325). v3's at_set takes any status from any status. This is v3 more OPEN and less faithful, not more closed." And `observed.exit` lists four exits, none of them a refusal for a wrong source status. ic ruled KEEP THE GUARD on 2026-08-15 at `20e8c4b3`, so the guard is owed and unbuilt -- the help string is v2's contract still being printed by v3.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE ROW. `--help` is the only contract most operators will ever read, and this one asserts a safety property that does not hold. It is also demonstrably contagious into documentation: it produced a false claim in two pages of the v3 doc set, written by someone who took the help string as the contract, and was caught only by accidentally exercising the verb.

POPULATION: 4 OF 118 SHIPPED ROWS assert a precondition or refusal in `help` (cc, 2026-08-29, detector positive-controlled both ways -- it catches `at green` and does not catch `st list`). `at green` FALSE. `ac new` and `at new` TRUE, built and asserted by tests. New-surface `organize` (previews unless `--apply`) UNVERIFIED and deliberately not driven, because settling a documentation question is not a reason to run an unverified write verb in a shared checkout during a release.

THE 4 IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING. The detector is a regex over English -- only from, refuses, requires, must, cannot, unless. A precondition phrased without one of those words is invisible to it.

THE OBVIOUS GATE CANNOT BE BUILT AS STATED, AND THIS IS THE PART TO READ BEFORE ANYONE TRIES. An arm that fails when a row's `help` asserts a precondition its `observed.exit` does not list is unbuildable: three of the four rows have NO `observed` block at all -- only `at green`, a v2-derived keep row, has one. Such an arm would fire on all three new-surface rows, two of which are true, or be inert on exactly the rows most likely to acquire the defect next, and its silence would read as a clean estate. Building a prose-regex gate for a population of four is also the ST0039 greppable-proxy shape: a mechanical check standing in for a judgement it cannot make.

THE REAL FIX IS STRUCTURAL AND IS ALREADY OWED. A dispatch-table row declares path, args, flags, target, disposition, recoverability, mcp exposure and read-or-mutate, and nothing structural about what it REFUSES. So the only place to state a refusal is prose, and prose in a `help` string is a contract nothing checks and nothing updates when the behaviour moves. Give refusals a declared home and `help` stops being a place a contract can be asserted at all -- the class closes rather than being policed. Until then the population is small enough to hand-check, and it is hand-checked above.

INTERIM: correct `at green`'s help so it describes what the verb does. Docs corrected at `cfe3ddbc`.

Driven by vc. Population, the three-field analysis, and the reason the gate is unbuildable are cc's.
